text.p: Summary of Consolidated Revenues and Income
Three Months Ended Six Months Ended

For the second quarter ended May 31, 1997, total revenues grew $2 million to $426 million, and net income increased 9% or $3 million to $37 million, compared to last years second quarter. Earnings per share increased 13% to $.54 compared to $.48 last year.

In the Health Care segment, Health Care sales were essentially flat compared with second quarter 1996 after excluding the impact of lower sales in Europe, primarily Germany, unfavorable currency adjustments and the disposition of Block Medical, the revenues of which were included in the second quarter of 1996. Health Care Sales gross profit margins improved 1.2 percentage points due to a shift in sales mix to higher-margin products, good cost controls and declining losses in our European operations. Health Care rental revenue was essentially flat as the increase in units in use in acute care, long term care and home care were offset by a change in mix, pricing pressures and lower European rentals. Health Care rentals gross profit margins grew 4.7 percentage points due to improved operating efficiency resulting from our continuous improvement efforts. Hill-Rom operating profit was down marginally as the improvement in gross profit was offset by increased investment in new product development.

In the Funeral Services segment, revenues grew as a result of increased casket and cremation urn shipments despite a lower death rate during the quarter. Good growth in new products in the wood and stainless steel casket lines, coupled with continued double-digit growth in cremation products, were responsible for the revenue increase. Funeral Services gross profit margins improved 1.5 percentage points due to good cost controls. Insurance revenues grew 23% and gross profit margins grew 1.6 percentage points as a result of higher levels of insurance in force, higher levels of investment income, and good control of operating expenses. Operating profit increased at double- digit rates for the Funeral Services Segment.

Year-to-date, total revenues grew 2% to $872 million, compared to the same period in 1996. Net income increased 13% to $76 million, and earnings per share increased 15% to $1.10, compared to $.96 in the same period in 1996.

"Although revenue growth continues to be soft due to continued economic weakness and reduced health care expenditures in Europe and a lower death rate in the United States, we are very pleased with margin improvements, cost controls and new product development. Aggressive new product development efforts by all of our business units cause us to remain optimistic about our future growth," said President and Chief Executive Officer, Gus Hillenbrand.
